There are strong, opposing opinions on whether the Electoral College should be abolished. Some argue it must be preserved to protect the interests of rural and small-town America, ensuring geographic balance and preventing presidential candidates from ignoring less populated states [d1, d3]. Others contend the system is undemocratic, outdated, and should be abolished because it allows candidates to win the presidency without winning the national popular vote, and it was founded on compromises related to slavery [d4, d5, d7, d8].
